object_description: two offset school buildings linked by a base wing
design_condition: Two offset buildings are positioned at right angles to the existing civic building, connected through a base wing and carefully stepped across different ground-floor heights to form graduated public and private outdoor sequences.

positive.statement: The project is seamlessly embedded in the district through a sensitive urban arrangement and a public outdoor space that feeds into the neighborhood.
The central break area cleverly combines the needs of the primary school and day school while connecting the school buildings and gymnasium.
The split-level organization subtly anchors the school in the site and creates unusual visual qualities.
The central hall and multifunctional music hall create a well-considered gesture toward the neighborhood.
The project handles the different ground-floor heights sensitively and creates a desired gradation in the publicity of outdoor spaces.
The two school buildings are precisely thought out and promise a well-functioning overall system.
The project performs well in energy efficiency through moderate spans, linear load transfer and coherent technical planning.
The construction costs fall within the middle range.

negative.statement: Access by ramps does not yet work.
The spatial richness and innovation of the primary-school section are not carried through to the core school and group-room typology.
The open central area creates a very large space that is sensitive in terms of acoustics.
The longitudinal classroom arrangement does not create flexible spaces for different forms of collaboration.
The basic-level building remains one-sided, and the quality of the upper-floor classrooms is not equally convincing.
The central toilet arrangement is unconvincing and storage options for school supplies are missing.
The caretaker's apartment appears unattractive because of its central, exposed location.
The complex roof landscape results in rather poor compactness.
The project does not fully fulfill its promise as a typological contribution to contemporary teaching.
